summary: Edge trace-merge at ingress produces stale routing shadow that bypasses pinned model
description:
Issue summary: After the recent edge ingress change that coalesces Zipkin/X-Ray trace IDs for trace continuity, BrightDocs observed a silent routing regression during canary traffic: tenant sessions that had an explicit model pin (redwood-open-13b-v2) were being routed to a degraded compatibility variant without any explicit fallback recorded. Impact: Several BrightDocs production requests returned mismatched outputs for ~2% of requests over a 30-minute window; customer reported incorrect semantic responses and a small billing spike due to retries. Environment: prod-us-west, BrightDocs tenant id bd-7631, Dedicated-inference pool (dedicated-3) running mixed spot/ondemand nodes.

Observed behavior: Edge trace-merge produces duplicated trace header patterns which correlate with a stale routing shadow lookup on the routing mesh; the routing mesh resolves to a legacy routing snapshot for those requests and skips pin enforcement. Expected behavior: Trace continuity should not alter routing snapshot selection or bypass explicit tenant model pinning.

Impact: P1/Sev1 for BrightDocs (enterprise SLA). Requests returned degraded variant silently; customer workflows relying on deterministic model behavior were affected.

Attachments/refs: link to Slack thread #support-brightdocs (https://slack.redwood/support-brightdocs), Kibana dashboard for tenant bd-7631, and the incident page (INC-2026-03-12-02).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Subscribe BrightDocs tenant to a staged canary with explicit pin to redwood-open-13b-v2. 2) Enable the new edge 'trace-coalesce' mode (the change rolled out yesterday). 3) Send steady traffic at 50 rps with a mix of short and long contexts. 4) Watch routing decisions on routing-mesh traces and cross-reference the trace IDs with edge ingress logs. 5) Reproduce observed fallback: requests with merged/duplicated trace headers resolve against an older routing snapshot and return compatibility variant outputs.

investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: trace coalescing at the edge reuses a trace ID namespace that collides with stale snapshot cache keys in routing-mesh, creating a 'shadow' lookup path that favors older snapshots. Evidence: correlated timestamps show mismatches between edge snapshot epoch (epoch-41) and current control-plane epoch (epoch-47) for impacted requests. We reproduced locally by forcing header x-trace values into an epoch-prefixed pattern; routing mesh returned older snapshot if trace header matched historic mapping.

Tech notes: routing-mesh uses a deterministic fingerprint that included an edge-generated trace-context for debug reconciliation. The recent change added trace coalescing to preserve parent/child continuity, but didn't scrub trace-context when computing snapshot fingerprint. This allowed trace collisions to select legacy fingerprints.

Telemetry: ~2% of BrightDocs traffic in us-west impacted, spike window 2026-03-12T18:08:00Z - 2026-03-12T18:38:00Z. No server 5xxs observed; fallbacks were silent (no error codes), which complicated detection.

Cross-references: SUP-3141592 (related canary fallback behavior), github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/4821 (edge trace coalesce change).

2026-03-12 18:38 - SRE (Ethan Morales): Confirmed correlation between merged trace headers and route_snapshot mismatch. Putting temporary mitigation: disable trace-coalesce on edge for prod-us-west and route-rollout freeze for BrightDocs tenant.

2026-03-12 19:05 - Platform Eng (Priya Singh): Reproduced locally. Root cause likely fingerprint includes x-trace header. Preparing PR to strip trace-context from fingerprint hash and add regression test.
2026-03-12 20:10 - Support (Maya Patel): Customer notified of mitigation (edge feature toggle rollback). BrightDocs acknowledged improved outputs after rollback.
resolution: Mitigation applied: disabled trace-coalesce on edge in prod-us-west at 2026-03-12T18:41Z for BrightDocs; unpin-safe rollouts paused. Root fix: patch routing-mesh fingerprint computation to ignore edge trace-context when computing snapshot fingerprint (PR #4853). Rollout plan: canary patch to routing-mesh + unit/regression tests, then staged rollout to prod-us-west. Postmortem to include stricter header sanitization in fingerprinting and an observability alert for silent fallback rate delta. Follow-up task: SUP-719003 to add unit tests and a synthetic monitor for silent fallback percentage.
next_steps: 1) Platform Eng to land PR (#4853) and run canary in staging by 2026-03-14. 2) QA to validate no regression for legitimate trace parent-child continuity. 3) Observability to add metric: 'silent_fallback_rate_by_tenant' and alert at >0.5% sustained. 4) Customer Success to follow up with BrightDocs with postmortem and credit reconciliation if needed.
public_notes: We disabled a new edge tracing coalescing feature for BrightDocs in us-west after detecting it could cause routing snapshot selection anomalies that bypassed pinned models. We have a patch to prevent trace headers from affecting routing fingerprints and are rolling it out in canary. We'll share a postmortem when complete.
related_consequences: Potentially affected tenants that had explicit model pins and were on edge nodes with trace-coalesce enabled in the same window. No data exfiltration or auth bypass observed. Billing spike due to retries recorded for BrightDocs; finance will review charge adjustments.
